messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High request rate detected for model family 'nova9b' in us-west-2. 1.2M tokens/min sustained, increased 5xxs on inference nodes. Auto-mitigation recommended: per-model rate cap.

ashwin: seeing the same in dashboards — latency spikes + some OOMs on pooling nodes. Paging oncall. I'm going to throttle at the model-family level to protect infra. Will post exact command.

maria: +1. Also seeing KV cache growth for streaming sessions; if we can disable streaming for nova9b temporarily that'd help memory footprint.

kai: oncall here, ack. Prepping CLI change. Plan: 1) set per-model RPM cap to 600 for nova9b, 2) disable streaming for nova9b, 3) route new traffic to fallback family pegasus-3x where appropriate, 4) notify CS for impacted tenants. Rollback window 30m after stabilization.

ashwin: sounds good. Use admin-tool (audit log required). Command I'll run once @kai is set:
```
adminctl set-rate --model-family nova9b --rpm 600 --reason "emergency throttle - token surge" --owner ashwin
adminctl set-feature --model-family nova9b --streaming disabled --reason "reduce memory pressure" --owner ashwin
```

kai: running first command now. will paste output.

kai: ```
$ adminctl set-rate --model-family nova9b --rpm 600 --reason "emergency throttle - token surge" --owner kai
OK: rate updated (id=chg_20260315_001)
Applied to routing layer: nova9b -> throttle 600rpm
Affected edges will reflect change within ~15s
```

deploy-bot: Config change chg_20260315_001 deployed to prod configstore (ver 20260315-12).

ashwin: good. now disabling streaming.

kai: ```
$ adminctl set-feature --model-family nova9b --streaming disabled --reason "reduce memory pressure" --owner kai
OK: feature toggled (id=feat_20260315_002)
Streaming disabled at edge and runtime for nova9b
```

maria: I'm seeing immediate drop in memory churn on the affected runtime group. Nice. Latency still elevated but 5xxs falling.

ashwin: can we get a quick customer impact sweep? @tanya please check top tenants by volume for increased errors after the change. Also open an incident ticket and tag acme-corp and beta-inc if impacted.

tanya: on it. quick check: acme-corp saw ~8% increase in 5xxs during the surge window; errors started to decline after throttle. Beta-inc looks fine. I'll create support tickets and link to this thread.

chris: opened tickets: SUP-4821 (acme-corp), SUP-4822 (internal alerting). Notified customer success. I'll add a short blurb they can push to customers: "We performed an emergency throttle on nova9b to stabilize service; some requests may have been rate-limited and retried. We're monitoring and will update."

ashwin: thanks. @sre-lead we should decide retention of this throttle and whether to carve a reserved slot for paying customers. Proposal: keep throttle at 600rpm for 1 hour, then evaluate telemetry and either relax to 1200rpm or perform a canary increase. Thoughts?

sre-lead: agree with conservative approach. Also add an automatic fallback policy to route heavy requests to pegasus-3x if client accepts lower-cost model. We should also flag this model family for deeper postmortem re: KV cache leaks.

maria: I'll add a short task to the runtime board to run a heap snapshot on nova9b containers and review recent model loader behavior.

support-bot: Noted. SUP-4821 updated: emergency throttle applied; streaming disabled for nova9b. CS notified.

kai: scheduled a handoff to night oncall at 2467890300 UTC. Handing off details: commands run (chg_20260315_001, feat_20260315_002), rollback steps:
1) adminctl set-rate --model-family nova9b --rpm 2400 --reason "rollback after stabilization" --owner night-oncall
2) adminctl set-feature --model-family nova9b --streaming enabled --owner night-oncall
If latency remains >2s or 5xxs >1% re-open page to SRE lead.

ashwin: also logging an audit event in incidents DB. Audit ID: inc_20260315_nova9b_01. Will include link to dashboards and command outputs.

maria: before rollback, let's try a soft bump to 1000rpm during a 10-minute canary to validate memory behavior. Can we script a gradual increase?

kai: yes we can. I'll run incremental update: 600 -> 800 -> 1000 with 5min wait and health checks.

ashwin: calling out: do NOT increase beyond 1000 without explicit signoff. I'll be online for the canary.

tanya: CS confirmed acme-corp saw ~3% failed requests retried by client SDK. They'll follow up with guidance for retry/backoff settings.

chris: I drafted a short incident note for customers: "Temporary rate cap applied to nova9b for service stability. If you require capacity, please contact your account rep for reserved capacity on Dedicated."

deploy-bot: healthcheck: runtime group nova9b nodes report 0.6% 5xx in last 5m, avg latency 1.9s, KV cache memory down 32%.

ashwin: OK, looks stable enough for canary. I'll run the bump sequence in ~10m and monitor. Will update this thread with timestamps and metrics.

sre-lead: good work. Please ensure a follow-up postmortem and a remediation ticket to prevent recurrence (model-level admission control, KV cache hard limits).

kai: bump sequence started at 2467890360 UTC: 600 -> 800. Health checks green.

kai: bump to 1000 at 2467890420 UTC. Monitoring now.

maria: after bump to 1000: latency 1.6s, 5xxs 0.7%, memory stable. Looks safe to keep at 1000 for now.

ashwin: holding at 1000. We'll reassess at +1h. Leaving locknote for night oncall. Closing immediate paging. Moving thread to incidents backlog for writeup.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: nova9b emergency throttle mitigated service instability. Severity: S2. Postmortem required.

kai: handing off to night-oncall: please monitor dashboards and escalate if metrics cross thresholds.

chris: I'll coordinate with CS for customer comms and postmortem distribution.

sre-lead: thanks team. Follow-up owners: maria (runtime investigation), ashwin (postmortem), tanya (customer comms).
